new_entities.name: Topical alpha hydroxy acids
new_entities.description: Topical alpha hydroxy acid formulations, especially glycolic-acid-based creams or peels, used to improve photoaged skin texture.

new_entities.name: Clinical skin texture
aliases: clinical skin roughness and fine-line appearance
new_entities.description: Clinically assessed skin texture, roughness, fine lines, and related visible surface features used in cosmetic dermatology trials.

edges.effect_quant: A 75-volunteer placebo-controlled trial of 5% glycolic acid improved general skin texture over 3 months, and a 30-woman prospective randomized study found glycolic acid reduced microsulcus number and width in the crow's-feet area. Later photodamage trials continued to show texture and fine-line benefits, although irritation rises with stronger acid regimens.
edges.population: adults with mild to moderate facial photoaging using low-strength glycolic-acid creams or professionally administered glycolic-acid regimens for weeks to months
edges.mechanism: Alpha hydroxy acids loosen corneocyte adhesion, increase epidermal turnover, and can smooth the stratum corneum enough to improve visible roughness and fine lines.
edges.summary: Topical alpha hydroxy acids do improve skin texture, but the effect is mostly surface-level and comes with a real irritation tradeoff. The evidence is consistent enough to rate the direction as beneficial, while keeping effect size modest.
edges.caveats: Texture gains are usually stronger than wrinkle-depth gains, and tolerance worsens as acid concentration or peel intensity rises. Trial endpoints vary widely between creams, peels, and mixed regimens.

evidence.notes: A double-blind randomized clinical trial on the effectiveness of a daily glycolic acid 5% formulation in the treatment of photoaging.

evidence.citation: RubinoC et al 2005 Plast Reconstr Surg
evidence.notes: A prospective study of anti-aging topical therapies using a quantitative method of assessment.

evidence.citation: RouvraisC et al 2018 J Cosmet Dermatol
evidence.notes: Antiaging efficacy of a retinaldehyde-based cream compared with glycolic acid peel sessions: A randomized controlled study.

effect_quant.comparator: crow's-feet wrinkle depth after glycolic-acid peel sessions
